title: Usage spike triage and billing snapshot
content:
Purpose:
This worksheet is a compact, repeatable triage and QBR-facing snapshot for unexpected token spend spikes and rate-limit incidents. Designed to be used live during QBR preparation and for rapid operational handoffs to SRE/finance.

How to use (3-minute playbook):
1) Paste the customer billing window and plan tier at the top.
2) Populate the quick metrics section from the billing export and metric queries (see sample queries below).
3) Run the diagnostics checklist in order; mark each step with a timestamp and owner.
4) If escalation is needed, use the provided Slack/email templates and fill in the variable fields.
5) Archive a copy of this snapshot in the customer folder and link back to the QBR doc.

Quick metrics snapshot (fill values):
- Customer: [customer-name]          Account ID: [acct-12345]
- Plan tier: [self-serve | committed | enterprise]
- Billing period: [YYYY-MM-DD to YYYY-MM-DD]
- Total token spend (period): [#### tokens]
- Median daily tokens (30d): [#### tokens/day]
- Peak day tokens (period): [#### tokens] at [timestamp]
- 1-hour spike tokens: [#### tokens] starting [timestamp]
- Active API keys: [#]    Active routes: [#]
- Rate-limit events (period): [#]    Distinct clients observed: [#]
- Charges projected (monthly run-rate): [$####]    Budget alert threshold: [$####]

Diagnostic checklist (ordered):
[ ] 1. Confirm billing export time range and currency conversion (Finance).
[ ] 2. Verify token accounting alignment: backend logs vs billing export (Eng infra).
[ ] 3. Check routing fallbacks — was traffic routed to a higher-cost region or variant? (Platform).
[ ] 4. Identify client(s) or API key(s) responsible for >60% of spike (CS -> provide customer context).
[ ] 5. Inspect request-level characteristics: sequence length, streaming vs non-streaming, embedding vs generation.
[ ] 6. Examine KV/prefix cache hit rate for the workload window (Serving runtime).
[ ] 7. Look for model switch/rollout events in the window (Product / Deployments).
[ ] 8. Verify if automatic batching configuration changed or if there was a sudden concurrency burst.
[ ] 9. Confirm there were no operational incidents (infra preemption, autoscaler flaps).
[ ] 10. Cross-check recent prompt/feature releases from the customer's product (CS notes).

Immediate containment actions (first 30–60 minutes):
- Enable temporary hard rate-limit on offending API key(s) with a 10–30% throttle to maintain availability while investigating.
- Apply per-route soft quota thresholds to prevent billing runaway (notify customer).
- Route future requests to a cheaper model variant (if acceptable for quality) and monitor error/latency impact.
- Turn on token-level logging for a 1-hour window with post-aggregation to preserve privacy.

Budget alert staging (recommended):
- Stage 1 (informational): 50% of committed monthly spend — automated email to customer and internal AM.
- Stage 2 (actionable): 75% — CS outreach + pre-approved throttling options suggested.
- Stage 3 (warning): 90% — automated low-latency token-limit kicks in unless customer confirms override.
- Stage 4 (escalation): 100%+ projected run-rate — finance-review + executive alert.

Suggested threshold numbers (example for a mid-market committed plan):
- 30-day median: 1.2M tokens/day
- Peak day threshold (alert): 2.5M tokens
- 1-hour spike threshold: 300k tokens
- Per-key rate-limit baseline: 20 reqs/min, burst 60 reqs/min -> adjust by route type

Sample SQL-ish queries / Metric snippets (adapt to internal schema):
- Total tokens by day: SELECT date_trunc('day', ts) as day, sum(tokens) FROM requests WHERE account_id='acct-12345' AND ts BETWEEN 'start' AND 'end' GROUP BY day ORDER BY day;
- Top API keys by tokens (24h): SELECT api_key, sum(tokens) as tokens FROM requests WHERE ts > now() - interval '24 hours' AND account_id='acct-12345' GROUP BY api_key ORDER BY tokens DESC LIMIT 20;
- Model variant token mix: SELECT model, sum(tokens) FROM requests WHERE ... GROUP BY model;

Customer-facing templates (fill variables)
- Slack/Email subject: "[Action required] Unexpected token surge on account [acct-12345] — quick triage"
- CS Slack body (short): Hi <customer_contact>, we observed a sudden increase in token volume (peak X tokens/hr) starting at <time>. We're throttling the top offender key to avoid billing overrun while we investigate. Expect a follow-up in 60 minutes with root cause.
- Escalation escalation-email: To: finance@redwood.com; Subject: Billing anomaly — acct-12345 projected +35% MoM; Body: includes snapshot table + preliminary responsible keys + proposed containment (hard-limit on key XYZ, route to model A-lite).

Stakeholder matrix (who to call when):
- CS lead (owner): Maya Rivera — customer context, business sensitivity, renewal signals.
- Eng infra: Jordan Patel — billing export validation, token reconciliation.
- Serving runtime: Priya Nair — cache/kv health, batching config.
- Platform/Deploys: Ethan Cole — model rollout/variant routing history.
- Finance: TBA (list finance rep) — charge projection and invoice adjustments.

Recording decisions for QBR notes (brief template):
- What happened (1-2 sentences): e.g., "On 2026-02-02 03:14 UTC, account X exceeded historical daily median by 420% driven by a new product feature that increased sequence length and concurrency."
- Root cause (summary): "Rapid A/B rollout + no per-key quota + model variant routing to higher-cost cluster."
- Mitigations taken: "Temporarily limited key ABC to 10 reqs/min; re-routed to cheaper variant; scheduled cache warm-up; committed to 24-hour follow-up."
- Long term action items: ordered list with owners and due dates.

Post-incident QBR checklist items:
- Add consolidated cost delta charts (30d, 90d) to QBR deck.
- Include a short appendix with the top 3 contributing routes/keys and customer feature mapping.
- Share the updated budget alert thresholds and confirm edit-access for CS/Finance.
- Propose a preventative guardrail: per-key debit balance or token pre-commit for heavy routes.

Notes / common pitfalls:
- Don’t rely on a single metric: spike in tokens can be sequence-length driven rather than user-count driven.
- Embeddings vs generation: embeddings may have higher per-request token counts; treat separately in analysis.
- Watch for time-zone mismatches between customer product logs and Redwood timestamps.

Appendix: severity decision table (guide)
- Sev1 (Critical billing exposure): projected >150% monthly run-rate, immediate throttle and exec alert.
- Sev2 (High): projected 100–150% run-rate, CS outreach, temporary throttles.
- Sev3 (Medium): one-off spike under 30% of monthly run-rate, monitor and follow up in QBR.

Last updated notes:
- 2025-09-03: initial draft (Maya)
- 2025-12-08: added budget staging thresholds and SQL snippets (Jordan)
- 2026-02-10: refined containment actions and Slack templates; changed severity table wording (Priya)

Action log (use this area to capture timestamps during triage):
- [2026-02-10 09:12 UTC] Maya: received alert from monitoring (peak tokens 420k/hr)
- [2026-02-10 09:15 UTC] Jordan: validated billing export; confirmed token delta matches backend logs
- [2026-02-10 09:22 UTC] Priya: applied soft per-key throttle on key-XYZ -> 30% reduction in sustained RPS
- [2026-02-10 09:45 UTC] Ethan: identified model variant switch at 08:58 UTC correlated to spike

End of snapshot. Save as: customer-success/Acct-[acct-12345]/billing-snapshots/YYYY-MM-DD and link from QBR deck.
